column62: The age of the complex is not well-constrained in the published literature. K-Ar biotite ages are 564±14 and 568 Ma from lamprophyre dikes, 575 Ma for nepheline syenite, unpublished Pb-Pb age from sphene, brookite, anatase, apatite, rutile ages of 550±4/576±3 with conflicting ages between published abstract and presentation according to Symons and and Chiasson (1991). The authors interpret the age of the complex to be 575±5 Ma, but this interpretation is rather qualitative.  Shafiqullah obtained two identical K-Ar biotite ages of 564 ± 14 Ma for the lamprophyre dikes (in Ferguson and Currie 1972). Currie (1976) reported K-Ar biotite ages of 568 Ma for a lamprophyre dike and 575 Ma for the nepheline syenite. Kamo et al. (1989b) reported a Pb-Pb isochron age using sphene, brookite, anatase, apatite, and rutile separates of 550 ± 4 Ma for a lamprophyre dike in an abstract, but they increased it to 576 ± 3 Ma on presentation. Overall, agreement between the K-Ar and Pb-Pb ages implies cooling of the pluton within a very few million years with no later metamorphism. Kamo et al., 1995 report a U-Pb unpublished zircon age of 577 ± 1 Ma for the syenite which would improve the constraints if used.

column62: Zhang et al. (2026, *Tectonics*) develop new U-Pb petrochronology and thermochronology datasets from zircon, garnet, titanite, rutile, and apatite from the Adirondack Highlands. Probabilistic thermal history inversion of these data shows that the Adirondack Highlands cooled slowly throughout the Tonian, with the magnetite-carried remanence in the Marcy Massif anorthosite acquired ca. **887 ± 23 Ma** — about 85 Myr later than the ca. 970 Ma cooling-curve estimate of Brown and McEnroe (2012). Zhang et al. additionally report a positive inverse baked-contact test in which an unmetamorphosed mafic dike (site GD1) bakes its anorthosite host (site MA11); because such dikes intrude Proterozoic but not Paleozoic rocks in the region (Fisher, 1977) and are correlated with Ediacaran dikes dated elsewhere in the Grenville Province (Kamo et al., 1995; Halls et al., 2015), the test demonstrates that the anorthosite magnetite remanence is Proterozoic in age. This revised age fills a critical gap in the Laurentia apparent polar wander path between the ca. 990 Ma Jacobsville Formation pole and the ca. 780 Ma Gunbarrel pole, with implications for the position of Rodinia in the early to mid-Tonian.

column62: The Torridon Group is poorly dated directly. Its youngest detrital zircons range from ca. 1070 to 1000 Ma (Applecross Formation: 1071 ± 55 Ma and 1060 ± 18 Ma; Aultbea Formation: 992 ± 52 Ma and 1046 ± 26 Ma; Rainbird et al., 2001; Krabbendam et al., 2017), and the absence of Cryogenian glacial deposits indicates deposition before ca. 717 Ma. A Grenvillian foreland-basin setting, correlation with the Morar Group metamorphosed at ca. 950-940 Ma during the Renlandian orogeny (Bird et al., 2018; Krabbendam et al., 2022), and whole-rock Rb-Sr ages of 994 ± 48 Ma and 977 ± 39 Ma interpreted as early diagenesis (Turnbull et al., 1996) favor deposition at ca. 1000-950 Ma. The pole is assigned **ca. 975 Ma (950-1050 Ma)**; in Laurentia coordinates it is quite similar to the ca. 990 Ma Jacobsville pole.

Heaman and Machado (1992) dated several centers by U-Pb (zircon/baddeleyite). The
**reversed-polarity** eastern gabbro (Center A) gives the most precise dates,
**1108 ± 1 Ma** and 1107 +5/−1 Ma, and the central nepheline syenite (Center C,

geochronology is not precise enough to fully resolve the emplacement history, but
it indicates that the reversed Centers A and C are the older (~1108 Ma) rocks and
the normal western rocks are younger, bracketing the single normal/reversed
polarity reversal recorded by the complex to ~1102–1105 Ma.

column62:
The SFM igneous province was originally dated at 1476 ± 16 Ma (U-Pb zircon;
Van Schmus et al., 1993), the age adopted by Meert & Stuckey (2002). A
subsequent U-Pb zircon and titanite study by du Bray et al. (2021) dated many
more SFM units and resolved two magmatic episodes: a more voluminous, widespread
episode at 1.48-1.45 Ga and a younger episode at 1.34-1.27 Ga. The dolerites and
acidic rocks carrying the paleomagnetic remanence belong to the older
1.48-1.45 Ga episode. Taking the spread of in-situ dates from that episode gives
a nominal age of 1466 Ma with bounds of 1448-1484 Ma, adopted here in place of
the older 1476 ± 16 Ma value.
